title: How do we draw the first steps of the snowflake?
description: The video draws the snowflake of Jia at Step zero, Step one and Step two on a triangle with sides of nine units. It puts a bump on the middle third of every side, counts the sides at each step, and checks the lengths of the new sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: at every step, each side gets a bump on its middle third and becomes four sides. Watch for students who put the bump only on the original three sides at Step two.

video_script.why: The child draws each step with the bump of the example in the book, on every side of the shape before.
video_script.substitution: Cut every side into three equal parts, raise a bump over the middle part, and count the sides.
video_script.anchor: the snowflake of Jia in the book, drawn at Step zero, Step one and Step two in three frames
video_script.payoff_line: Step one is a star with twelve sides, and Step two has forty eight sides

final_answer.value: Step 0 has 3 sides, Step 1 is a star with 12 sides, Step 2 has 48 sides
final_answer.spoken: Step zero has three sides. Step one is a star with twelve sides, and Step two has forty eight sides

names.Jia: Swedish mathematician who described the snowflake in 1904

hold_back: Answer: Step 0 has 3 sides, Step 1 is a star with 12 sides, Step 2 has 48 sides
never_show: a Step 2 drawing with bumps only on the original three sides
maths_rules: Step 0: equilateral triangle with sides of 9 units on dot paper, 3 sides
Step 1: each side is cut into 3 parts of 3 units, a bump is raised over the middle part; 3 x 4 = 12 sides, a six pointed star
Step 2: each of the 12 sides is cut into 3 parts of 1 unit, a smaller bump is raised; 12 x 4 = 48 sides
check: each Step 2 side is 3 / 3 = 1 unit, a third of the Step 1 side
video_script.design: Three frames in a row on the stage. Each frame is drawn in turn, and the number of sides is written under it.
